name: Is bathroom tile waterproof by itself?

mainEntity.name: Is bathroom tile waterproof by itself?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tile and standard grout are not waterproof on their own. While glazed tile sheds surface water, standard cement-based grout and stone are porous materials that absorb moisture. In addition, routine building movement creates hairline cracks in grout lines over time, allowing water to penetrate behind the decorative surface. Without a continuous waterproof membrane applied directly to cement boards or a dedicated waterproof substrate system, moisture reaches framing, subfloors, and adjacent drywall. Relying solely on surface sealers or grout will eventually cause subsurface damage and adhesive failure in wet areas.
acceptedAnswer.description: No, tile and cement grout are porous and do not stop water on their own. A dedicated waterproof membrane behind the tile is required to protect framing and subfloors.
